description: Composite four-panel figure on the hot deformation behaviour of Fe-Mn-Al-C steel (Gleeble-3500 rheological/flow-stress data). (a) True stress (MPa, 0-300, ticks at 0/100/200/300) versus True strain (0.0-1.0, ticks 0.0-1.0 by 0.2) at a fixed strain rate of 0.01 s^-1 for six labelled temperatures: 900 °C (black), 950 °C (red), 1000 °C (blue), 1050 °C (magenta), 1100 °C (green), 1150 °C (dark blue). Every curve rises to a peak then softens to a plateau; the 900 °C curve peaks just above the 300 MPa gridline, the 1150 °C curve stays near 40 MPa. (b) True stress (MPa, 0-250, ticks by 50) versus True strain (0.0-1.0) at T = 1100 °C for four strain rates: 10 s^-1 (magenta), 1 s^-1 (blue), 0.1 s^-1 (red), 0.01 s^-1 (black); peak height falls from just above 225 MPa to about 65 MPa as strain rate decreases. (c) 3D surface map of Peak stress (MPa) versus Strain rate/s^-1 (0.01-0.1) and Temperature/°C (900-1150), colour bar 53.00-394.0 MPa. (d) Same type of 3D peak-stress map for strain rate 1-10 s^-1, colour bar 94.00-486.0 MPa. Panels (c) and (d) show peak stress rising steeply with falling temperature and rising strain rate.

subfigures.description: True stress vs True strain curves (0-300 MPa; strain 0.0-1.0) at strain rate 0.01 s^-1, labelled 900, 950, 1000, 1050, 1100 and 1150 °C. All curves peak early (peak strain about 0.1-0.2) then soften to a plateau; the 900 °C curve peaks just above the 300 MPa gridline and the 1150 °C curve sits near 40 MPa.

True stress vs True strain curves (0-250 MPa; strain 0.0-1.0) at T = 1100 °C, labelled 10, 1, 0.1 and 0.01 s^-1. The 10 s^-1 curve peaks above the 225 MPa level and softens slightly; 1 s^-1 peaks near 155 MPa, 0.1 s^-1 near 100 MPa, 0.01 s^-1 near 65 MPa, the latter two being almost flat after the peak.

3D surface plot of Peak stress/MPa against Strain rate/s^-1 (labelled 0.10, 0.08, 0.06, 0.04, 0.02 in the low-rate range) and Temperature/°C (900-1150). Colour bar from 53.00 (violet) to 394.0 MPa (dark red). Peak stress is low (violet/green) at high temperature and low strain rate, rising steeply toward the red corner.

3D surface plot of Peak stress/MPa (100-500 MPa axis) against Strain rate/s^-1 (1-10) and Temperature/°C (900-1150). Colour bar from 94.00 (violet) to 486.0 MPa (dark red). The surface is uniformly high (red) at low temperature, dropping sharply as temperature approaches 1150 °C.

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots true stress-true strain curves at a fixed strain rate of 0.01 s^-1 for six temperatures labelled 900, 950, 1000, 1050, 1100 and 1150 °C, with axes True stress/MPa (0-300) and True strain (0.0-1.0).
In panel (a) the flow stress level decreases monotonically with increasing temperature: the 900 °C curve peaks just above the 300 MPa gridline while the 1150 °C curve remains near 40 MPa.
Every curve in panels (a) and (b) displays a single peak at low strain (approximately 0.1-0.2) followed by flow softening to a steady plateau, the classic dynamic-recrystallization flow shape.
Panel (b) plots true stress-true strain curves at T = 1100 °C for strain rates 10, 1, 0.1 and 0.01 s^-1; peak stress falls from just above 225 MPa (10 s^-1) to about 65 MPa (0.01 s^-1).
Panel (c) is a 3D surface map of peak stress (MPa) versus strain rate (low-rate range around 0.01-0.1 s^-1) and temperature (900-1150 °C) with a colour bar running from 53.00 to 394.0 MPa.

Panel (d) is a 3D surface map of peak stress versus strain rate (1-10 s^-1) and temperature (900-1150 °C) with a colour bar running from 94.00 to 486.0 MPa; its colour-bar maximum is higher than that of panel (c), consistent with higher peak stresses in the high-strain-rate regime.
Both 3D maps (c) and (d) show peak stress increasing steeply toward the low-temperature, high-strain-rate corner and decreasing toward the high-temperature, low-strain-rate corner.
The caption defines the panel conditions: (a) strain rate = 0.01 s^-1; (b) T = 1100 °C; (c) strain rate = 0.01-0.1 s^-1; (d) strain rate = 1-10 s^-1.

The citation states that the rheological stress behaviour is primarily influenced by T and strain rate, and that the steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material.
The citation reports that at the low strain rate (0.01 s^-1) the peak stress decreases from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C, a reduction of 82%.
The citation reports that at the high strain rate (10 s^-1) the peak stress decreases by 73% within the same 900-1150 °C temperature range.

The citation attributes the temperature dependence to faster grain-boundary mobility, stronger DRX/DRV softening and lower dislocation-slip resistance at higher T, and the strain-rate dependence to shortened deformation time giving insufficient DRV/DRX and stronger work hardening.
